$comment: SOURCE OF TRUTH for the Loom community-JSON specification version.
Every document under docs/references/ declares, in its YAML frontmatter, the spec version it was
written against. A doc whose declared version differs from `current` below is STALE and must be
re-verified before the Skill is allowed to rely on it. See _meta/publishing-flow.md.
ONE number versions the whole package -- see `versionField` below and
_meta/versioning-policy.md. This is enforced by DocsSyncChecker, which runs as a test.
It was previously a convention that nothing executed, and it drifted three times.
ONE version for the whole JSON specification, at package root.
Replaces schemaVersion, experience.experienceSchemaVersion and
experience.workflowGrammarVersion, which no package should carry any more.
Starts at 4 deliberately: strictly greater than every value any of the
three legacy fields ever held, so a numeric comparison across the two
schemes cannot be misread. The distinct field name is what actually
disambiguates; the value is belt and braces.
versionField.bumpRule: Breaking changes only, exactly as before -- an additive change (a new formula function, effect op, guard kind, or cardSurfaceFamily) does not bump. This is what stops a single number making every file spuriously old.

$comment: FROZEN HISTORY, not live. Until specVersion 4 the package carried three
independent version numbers. They are recorded here so the provenance of
older packages stays readable, and so the reasoning below is not lost.
Why they were collapsed: three numbers were meant to keep the blast radius
honest, but nothing enforced them -- docs-sync-checker.md was specified and
never built, and it predicted this outcome in its own opening line. The
result was drift three times over: the CommunityVoteApi docs that survived
the API's deletion; grammar 2 shipping into every fixture's CONTENT while
all 13 kept declaring 1 for four months; and an identity rename that
renamed keys in all three layers while bumping only one.
A change to any component now bumps the version of the whole package.
legacyLayers.grammarNote: Grammar was mid-flight at 3 (the roleId/fanId identity split) when the collapse happened. That change ships as specVersion 4.

statusReason: PROVISIONAL, not frozen. Phase A.5 now parses the engine-native experience schema (v2), registers
its definitions, and seeds its instances into one shared runtime engine per extension. It is not yet
rendered by the running app; the generic card through live UI gates are Phase A.6-A.10. Phase A
ends in a deliberate human review gate whose EXPECTED outcome is that this specification changes.
Do not treat any version number here as stable until Phase A's gate closes and this file's status
flips to `stable`. Until then, docs in this tree describe an intended contract, verified against
the engine's parser and evaluator and the app-shell parser, but not yet end-to-end in the running UI.

resolvedQuestions.$comment: Open questions settled by reading the source, recorded so they are not re-litigated.
resolvedQuestions.stringLiteralsInFormulas: RESOLVED 2026-07-14: string literals ARE supported, in both single and double quotes (formula_evaluator.dart:540). "availabilityState == 'available'" is valid. This was previously listed as an unknown.
resolvedQuestions.unaryNotOperator: CORRECTED 2026-07-17: `negationOperators` below previously claimed BOTH `!` and `!=` are absent. Verified directly against the parser: only `!=` is actually absent (`_comparison()`, formula_evaluator.dart:428-436, never checks for it). Unary `!` genuinely works -- parsed by `_unary()` (:458-462) and evaluated (`!_bool(v)`, :236). `formulas.md` corrected to match.

resolvedInGrammar.$comment: Gaps that were in knownGaps and are now fully closed -- grammar, engine execution, AND validator coverage all confirmed. Moved here 2026-07-16 per the publishing flow (_meta/publishing-flow.md step 8), rather than deleted, so the resolution is traceable.
resolvedInGrammar.transitionInputs: GAP-1, RESOLVED 2026-07-16. `transitions[].inputs` + `{input.x}` interpolation + `renderBindings[].repeater.itemActions` are implemented and validated. Real engine execution confirmed: `applyTransition` accepts `inputs`, refuses when a `required` one is missing, and `{input.x}` resolves inside effects (including recursively in nested List/Map effect values) -- proven end-to-end by `tournament-ballot.cast-vote` in the frozen Tabletop Club JSON (two concurrent-shaped calls with different `choice` values produce two distinct, non-racing `tournament-vote` rows). Validator adds `unknown_input_type`, `unknown_input_reference`, `unknown_item_reference`. See `app/packages/core/loom_workflow_engine/lib/src/models/workflow_models.dart` (`LoomWorkflowTransition.inputs`, `RepeaterSpec`/`RepeaterItemAction`), `effect_evaluator.dart` (`{input.x}`), `local_workflow_engine_api.dart` (`applyTransition`'s required-input check).
resolvedInGrammar.queryBackedSources: GAP-4, RESOLVED 2026-07-16. `instanceDataSchema[].source` (`query(type where foreignField == localField)`) is now genuinely parsed (`source_query.dart`) AND executed: `_hydrateSourceFields` runs the bounded equality query against the real store and populates the field with full matched-row instance data, wired into every read path that materializes instance data for a caller (`queryInstances`, `availableTransitionsAsync`, `applyTransition`'s result, `dueNotifications`). Proven end-to-end: `tournament-ballot.ballots` (source-backed) now populates for real, and its already-existing, unchanged formulas (`voteCounts`/`winner`/`tiedCandidates`/`isTie`) compute correctly over it. Also required implementing `{id}` interpolation (the acting instance's own id) -- a related, previously-undiscovered gap the frozen JSON's `cast-vote` effect (`"ballotId": "{id}"`) depended on but nothing implemented; see `effect_evaluator.dart`/`local_workflow_engine_api.dart`. Validator adds `invalid_source_query_syntax`, `dangling_source_query_workflow_type`, and widens `computed_field_written_by_effect`/`computed_field_seeded` to also cover `source`-backed fields (previously only checked `formula`).
resolvedInGrammar.styleFieldBinding: RESOLVED 2026-07-24 (CALR.9b, commit f4bf58f). `RenderBinding.styleField` now genuinely parses (mirrors `audienceMemberField`'s pointer-field pattern) and the App Shell genuinely consumes it: `stylePaletteFrom(accent)` derives six related-but-distinct colors from one community accent via systematic HSL hue rotation, and a single shared `_calendarEntryStyleColor` resolver reads `instanceData[binding.styleField]` to index that palette for the Calendar agenda row's fill and the month-grid/week-strip event-title dot -- falling back to the flat accent for any binding that doesn't declare `styleField`. Proven end-to-end on the real frozen fixture: Friday game night (`cardStyleId` 2) and Summer tournament (`cardStyleId` 1) render in genuinely distinct, accent-derived colors. Independently verified: 118/118 App Shell + 141/141 engine tests, 0 analyzer issues. Moved out of `proposedNotImplemented` (was stale there) per this file's own rule that the code wins on disagreement.
resolvedInGrammar.editGuard: RESOLVED 2026-07-25 (CALR.10a, commits 494f4cb..5ce77bd, 5 rounds). `LoomWorkflowState.editGuard` genuinely parses as a nullable `WorkflowGuard?`, deliberately staying `null` (not `WorkflowGuard()`'s open default) when absent from JSON. Calendar's real detail card (`_EventRsvpDetailCard`, not `GenericWorkflowInstanceCard`) reads it before rendering real, type-aware editors + a working Save button, calling `engine.updateInstanceFields`. Independent verification caught and closed a real Save-persistence bug the sandbox's own self-reports missed across 5 rounds -- final root cause was the Calendar dispatcher's post-mutation requery racing the write and briefly showing stale data, fixed with a local, card-scoped stale-guard (no shared-dispatcher changes). Confirmed live on a real Android emulator: organizer sees and can save real edits; member sees none. Independently verified: 120/120 App Shell + 143/143 engine tests, 0 analyzer issues.
resolvedInGrammar.calendarDateRailBinding: RESOLVED 2026-07-25 (CALR.10b, commits f3dbc15/2e0c12b, 2 rounds). `theme.calendar.dateRail.entries` genuinely parses into `LoomExperienceDefinition.calendarDateRailEntries` and the App Shell genuinely renders it: `dateToken` entries via pure date arithmetic, `formula` entries via the real formula evaluator over a `dayInstances` binding, `colorSource: styleField` reusing CALR.9b's style-slot palette. All three render primitives (`label`/`circleHighlight`/`badge`) implemented, with `circleHighlight` carefully preserving the exact today-only-filled-circle rule so every community that doesn't opt in renders pixel-identical to before. Rail width halved 96->48 as a separate, unconditional change. Confirmed live: the real frozen fixture's 3-entry example (including a `count(dayInstances)` badge) renders correctly on a real Android emulator. Independently verified: 122/122 App Shell + 143/143 engine tests, 0 analyzer issues.
resolvedInGrammar.transitionRelatedEffect: RESOLVED 2026-07-25 (CAL.WaitlistPromotion, commit e188463, 2 rounds). A new effect op (`effects.md` op 11) letting a transition find a queried set of sibling instances of another workflow type (`relatedQuery`: same `filter` shape as `guards.md`'s `relatedAggregate`, plus `sortKey`/`limit`) and apply a named `transitionId` to the first match after sorting -- closing the one remaining cross-instance gap (`relatedInstance`/cross-instance `set` only write one field on one directly-named instance; `createInstance` only spawns new ones). Semantics are a real `applyTransition` call: the target's own guard is evaluated fresh, and a guard failure is a silent no-op, not an error, letting the effect attach unconditionally to every transition that might free a seat. Required a real architectural fix along the way: `applyTransition` is now split into a read-only `_resolveTransition` phase (guard checks + GAP-1 input validation, deliberately outside any database transaction, restoring its original design after a fix-round caught a real regression -- nesting that check inside the transaction caused `SqliteException: cannot start a transaction within a transaction` on a second call) and `_applyTransitionWithinTransaction` (effect application + state update, callable by a caller that already owns a transaction) -- this is what lets `transitionRelated` apply a real, guard-respecting transition to another instance from inside the same outer transaction with no nesting. Landed in the frozen fixture: `event-rsvp-response`'s `respond-maybe`/`respond-declined` transitions promote the oldest (`rsvpedAt`-sorted) waitlisted row to `going`. Both real validators re-run clean (0/0). Independently verified: 147/147 engine tests, 114/114 validator tests, 0 analyzer issues.
resolvedInGrammar.generateRecurringInstancesEffect: RESOLVED 2026-07-25 (CAL.Recurrence, 7 milestones, commits 2974310/e653074 engine, 91ef180 validator, f5d30b9/b4ee5c2 frozen fixture, 7128d9a App-Shell creation UI, 4eb10d8 App-Shell delete-series). New effect op (`effects.md` op 12): a `make-recurring` transition on `event-rsvp` (orthogonal, `to: null`, self-removing via `formula: "seriesId == null"`) mints one `seriesId`, stamps it onto the anchor instance in place (occurrence 0), and creates `count - 1` real, independent sibling instances via bespoke Dart date arithmetic (`recurrence_evaluator.dart`) -- not the formula evaluator, since full pattern generality (daily/weekly-by-weekday/monthly-by-date-with-clamping/monthly-by-last-or-Nth-weekday) is real month-boundary arithmetic that would over-generalize that language for one narrow feature. Engine round found and fixed two real bugs before the fixture could safely use it: an omitted optional `recurrenceRule` field resolved to a garbage literal token string instead of `null` (`resolveEffectValue`'s `{input.x}` exact-match branch only handled the key-present case); and the weekly `byDayOfWeek` walk assumed occurrence 0 always equals the anchor, false whenever the anchor's own weekday isn't itself requested. Validator round found a real validator/engine mismatch the original ticket missed (`recurrence_weekday_without_set_pos` -- the engine already rejected monthly `byDayOfWeek` without `bySetPos`, but nothing asked the static validator to catch it). App-Shell: `_RecurrenceRulePickerDialog` (freq/interval/count + freq-conditional fields, only including a key when actually set) plus the required, easy-to-miss follow-up -- per-member `event-rsvp-response` rows are seeded by App-Shell code, not the engine, so every generated sibling needed its own seeding pass (pagination-based sibling lookup, mirroring `EngineNativeBindingDispatcher._load`'s cycle-guard loop). Deleting one occurrence needed no new capability (today's existing `cancel-event`, unchanged); deleting an entire series is App-Shell client orchestration (same pagination + a loop over `cancel-event`), not a new engine bulk-op. Independently verified end-to-end on the real frozen fixture: `loom_workflow_engine` 159/159, `loom_ux_judges` 119/119, `loom_communities_app_shell` 128/128, 0 analyzer issues across all three packages, both real validators (`community_package_validator.dart`, `workflow_state_machine_validator.dart`) clean against the updated fixture.
resolvedInGrammar.combineDateAndTimeFormula: IMPLEMENTED 2026-08-01 (Notifications Experience phase, CAL.Notify2.9). `combineDateAndTime(date, time)` is a public formula function backed by the shared value-parsing logic used by the `cancellationDeadline`/`locationOverlap` guards. It accepts an evaluated ISO date value and optional `HH:mm` value, returns local midnight when time is absent/null, and fails closed for missing or malformed values. The real validator accepts the function through the engine's formula vocabulary, enabling the frozen `event-rsvp`/`tournament-event` `reminderAt` computed fields.
resolvedInGrammar.calendarReminderApi: IMPLEMENTED 2026-08-01 (Notifications Experience phase, CAL.Notify2.9). `event-rsvp`/`tournament-event` now compute `reminderAt` from their event date/time and offset, while `event-rsvp-response` retains the engine-enforced `reminderSentAt` idempotency stamp. Calendar performs a client-orchestrated live-refresh check for each viewer's response row; when `now() >= reminderAt` and the row is eligible and unstamped, it creates a real `notification` row through the existing delivery choke point and applies `send-reminder` to stamp the response. The automatic Calendar action-chip row hides that internal transition; no Calendar-specific reminder UI is added.

groundedIn.$comment: The code this specification is derived from. If any of these change, this spec may be stale.

knownGaps.$comment: Capabilities the docs describe as needed but the grammar does NOT yet support. Each must be closed or explicitly deferred before the Skill (Phase 3) can rely on this spec. GAP-1 and GAP-4 moved to `resolvedInGrammar` above, 2026-07-16.
knownGaps.instanceCreation: GAP-2 (LARGELY RESOLVED 2026-07-21; tab-scoped surface now proven across every real archetype, 2026-08-05). Grammar/model + tab-scoped UI are done. Grammar v2 (2026-07-21) replaced the flat `renderBindings[].creatable` object with an `actions[]` array (see grammar layer values.2 and proposedNotImplemented.actionsGrammar). Tab-scoped `create` actions are fully built and shipping end-to-end: `event-rsvp` (New event, CALR.3-3h2), `tournament-event` (New tournament, CALR.3b), and every other tab-level creation runs through the real generic creation pipeline (GenericWorkflowCreationCard via EngineNativeArchetypeCreationCard's cardSurfaceFamily dispatch), verified by full-suite tests. Tracker 3 Phases E and F additionally proved this pipeline on `game-purchase-proposal` (Propose a game) and `discussion-thread` (New thread), and Phase F added `personaId[]`-typed creation-field support (AudienceMultiSelectPicker), so tab-scoped creation is no longer Calendar-only infrastructure -- every one of Tabletop Club's six real tabs now has at least one working tab-scoped create action. What REMAINS is the instance-scoped surface (scope: instance -- a card `button` or a contextual FAB, with `{context.*}` resolution from the in-focus/owning instance), tracked in proposedNotImplemented.actionsGrammar and the tracker's CALR.4a-f rows.
knownGaps.listMinusActor: GAP-3 (non-blocking). 'All participants except the actor' is not expressible -- no set-difference effect op. Consequence: thread unread state is a single bool rather than per-persona. Proposed: `setFromFormula` effect op + a `removeAll(list, value)` formula function. Additive. Deferred, non-blocking Phase F capability -- not attempted in Phase A'.
knownGaps.responseModel: The `responseModel: { kind: simpleRsvp }` sugar in V2's Calendar_RSVP design doc is NOT parsed by the engine. RSVP must be modeled with plain transitions + effects + formulas instead.
knownGaps.negationOperators: CORRECTED 2026-07-17 (see resolvedQuestions.unaryNotOperator) -- only `!=` is actually absent from the formula grammar; unary `!` genuinely works. Invert `!=` by restructuring: `if(a == b, false, true)` instead of `a != b`. Confirmed by reading the parser (formula_evaluator.dart:428-436).
knownGaps.rankTopN: `rank` / `topN` named functions are proposed in ComputationModel.md but unimplemented. `sortBy` covers the same need.
knownGaps.powExp: `pow` / `exp` are not implemented (would be required for a true Elo expected-score calculation).
knownGaps.stringConcatenation: Formulas cannot concatenate strings. Use `labelTemplate` (e.g. "{value} seats") for display composition instead.

proposedNotImplemented.$comment: NEW grammar/engine surface designed 2026-07-17 for the Calendar redesign (event-rsvp per-row response table, Day/Week/Month/Pending views, real event creation). Fully specified and written into the frozen JSON + reference docs, but NONE of it is engine- or App-Shell-implemented yet -- tracked separately from knownGaps because these are net-new proposals, not gaps in an existing contract. See docs/references/communities/tabletop-club.md section 11's 2026-07-17 review-log row for the full context and the CAL/AS ticket gap list for implementation scope.
proposedNotImplemented.createInstances: New method on the ABSTRACT WorkflowEngineApi (not Local-only, unlike the existing install-time-only seedInstances) -- atomic bulk-create, needed so an event's per-member event-rsvp-response rows can be created as one real API operation, not N racy individual createInstance calls.
proposedNotImplemented.relatedAggregateGuard: New guard kind 7 (guards.md) -- a live count/sum/etc. over a related table compared to a threshold, evaluated by the caller pre-computing the aggregate via the existing real aggregate() method before the still-synchronous evaluateGuard runs.
proposedNotImplemented.stateReservedColumn: `$state` (formulas.md) -- exposes a query-backed row's own current FSM state to `groupCount`/aggregate functions. Requires `_readAllInstancesOfType` (and therefore `aggregate()` and GAP-4 hydration) to merge in the row's `currentState`, which today only exposes raw `instanceData`.
proposedNotImplemented.subtractHoursFunction: New formula function (formulas.md) -- date arithmetic (subtract an hour count from a date), needed to compute tournament-ballot.dueAt as a real computed field instead of a hand-seeded, driftable value.
proposedNotImplemented.mapGetFunction: New formula function (formulas.md) -- pull one value out of a map (e.g. a groupCount tally) by key, defaulting to 0 if absent.
proposedNotImplemented.responseTableBinding: New render-binding key (render-bindings.md) -- points a calendar-family archetype at its per-member response table generically, instead of the App Shell hardcoding field names.
proposedNotImplemented.filterableFacetsBinding: New render-binding key (render-bindings.md) -- named, labeled, computed-field-backed filters/stats a generic list surface may offer.
proposedNotImplemented.creatableActionExperienceField: NEW 2026-07-20, IMPLEMENTED 2026-07-20/21 (CALR.3g/3h1/3h2/3b). `experience.creatableAction` (community-wide defaults) + `experience.tabCreatableActionStyles` (per-tab override, same cascade shape as theme/tabThemes), each holding two independently-resolving fields: `multiActionStyle` (speedDial/stacked/singleFirst -- how multiple tab-scoped create-actions on one tab lay out) and `presentationStyle` (popup/slideOutBottom/slideOutLeft/slideOutRight -- how the launched creation form presents). `popup` uses the official Flutter-team `animations` package's `OpenContainer` (container-transform motion). All three multiActionStyle values and all four presentationStyle values ship end-to-end and are full-suite tested. As of grammar v2 these fields govern `actions[]` entries with `scope: "tab"` (see values.2). Retained here (not moved to resolvedInGrammar) only because this whole spec file is still `provisional`.
proposedNotImplemented.actionsGrammar: NEW 2026-07-21 (grammar v2), EXTENDED 2026-07-21 with a second action kind. Replaced the flat `renderBindings[].creatable` object with an `actions[]` array of two kinds sharing one shape. `kind: "create"`: `label`, `byPersonaIds`, optional `workflowType` (defaults to the binding's own type; set for the cross-archetype case, e.g. a tournament-event-owned action that creates a tournament-ballot), `scope` (`tab` default | `instance`), `presentation` (`fab` default | `button`), and `prefill`. Scope is the whole model: tab-scoped = brand-new instance, always a tab FAB, no `{context.*}`, visible even with zero instances; instance-scoped = related to a specific instance, renders as a card `button` (context = that card's instance) or a contextual `fab` (context = the in-focus instance via the App Shell's existing focus tracker), needs at least one host instance to appear. `{context.id}` = the host instance's own id; `{context.<field>}` = its instanceData field. `kind: "transition"`: names an already-declared `transitions[].id` (`transitionId`, required) on the binding's own workflow type and gives it a distinguished presentation (fab/button) instead of the automatic button row -- removing only that one transition from the row, leaving every other transition rendering automatically as before. `scope` is fixed to `instance` (a transition always acts on an existing instance); `byPersonaIds`/`workflowType`/`prefill` are inapplicable (the transition's own `guard` and `inputs` remain the sole source of truth for eligibility and target type); use `inputs` (not `prefill`) to pass values into `applyTransition`, which may reference `{context.<field>}` as a self-reference to the instance being transitioned. IMPLEMENTED: scope:tab creates (the tab creatable-action FAB -- see creatableActionExperienceField). NOT YET IMPLEMENTED: scope:instance creates (button + contextual FAB + `{context.*}` resolution + excluding instance-scoped actions from the tab FAB), the entire `kind: "transition"` surface, and the grammar-v2 validator rules (unknown_action_kind/scope/presentation, tab_action_cannot_be_button, dangling_action_workflow_type, dangling_action_transition_id, transition_action_cannot_be_tab_scoped, transition_action_cannot_set_workflow_type/prefill/by_persona_ids, unknown_action_input_reference, duplicate_action_transition_id, create_action_cannot_set_inputs, context_reference_outside_instance_action). Tracked in the tracker's CALR.4a-f rows. See render-bindings.md `actions` section for the full grammar.
proposedNotImplemented.creationGuardStateKey: NEW 2026-07-26 (CAL.Calendar2 design pass -- CAL.Calendar2.0/2.9). `states[].creationGuard: WorkflowGuard?` (workflow-grammar.md) gates instance creation itself, closing a real gap found during this pass: `createInstance`/`createInstances`/`_createInstanceValidated` (`local_workflow_engine_api.dart`) run zero guard checks today, only schema validation. Reuses the exact `WorkflowGuard` type `editGuard`/`transitions[].guard` already use -- no new guard shape -- but its absent-default is the OPPOSITE of `editGuard`'s: absent means open (the normal guards.md default), not closed, since virtually every existing creatable workflow type depends on staying open with no guard declared at all. Checked at the one shared choke point every creation path already funnels through, so a `locationOverlap` creationGuard automatically covers every sibling `generateRecurringInstances` spawns too.
proposedNotImplemented.editGuardEngineEnforcement: NEW 2026-07-26 (CAL.Calendar2.0). Real authorization gap found during the CAL.Calendar2 audit: `editGuard` (resolvedInGrammar.editGuard above) is only consulted by the App Shell's `_editableKeys` getter to decide whether to render editors -- `updateInstanceFields` itself never calls `evaluateGuard` against it, only checking `editableFields`/`writableBy`/`formula`-absence. A client bypassing the UI (or a future automation) could edit organizer-only fields directly today. Proposed fix: `updateInstanceFields` evaluates `editGuard` the same way `applyTransition` evaluates transition guards, refusing (not silently allowing) when it fails or is unset for a state with non-empty `editableFields`.
proposedNotImplemented.relatedAggregateFieldParam: NEW 2026-07-26 (CAL.Calendar2.8). Closes a real, previously undocumented bug found during the CAL.Calendar2 audit: `guards.md`'s `relatedAggregate` kind 6 documents `sum`/`avg`/`min`/`max`/`countDistinct` as available, but `RelatedAggregateGuard` has no field/column parameter and `_passesRelatedAggregateGuard` hardcodes `column: ''` when calling the real `aggregate()` method, which requires a genuine column for every op but `count`. Today, any of those five ops silently aggregates over an empty string and produces a meaningless result -- not an error. Adds a `field` parameter to `RelatedAggregateGuard`, wired through to `aggregate()`'s real `column` argument. Needed for CAL.Calendar2.8's party-size feature (`op: "sum"` over a `partySize` field) but is a correctness fix independent of it. FIXTURE UPDATED 2026-07-29: `respond-going`'s capacity guard now declares `op: "sum", field: "partySize"` and `event-rsvp-response` gained a `partySize` field (required GAP-1 input, all 14 seeded response rows backfilled with `partySize: 1`) -- deliberately landing atomically with this engine fix in the same implementation pass, never shipped ahead of it (the JSON alone is inert/silently-wrong exactly as described above until the engine change lands too).
proposedNotImplemented.cancellationDeadlineGuard: NEW 2026-07-26 (CAL.Calendar2.2). Guard kind 8 (guards.md) -- `{ dateField, timeField?, hoursBefore }`, combining a date and (optional) time field into a real timestamp before comparing against `now() - hoursBefore hours`. Deliberately a dedicated, typed guard kind rather than a `formula` string: `eventDate` alone parses to midnight (`formula_evaluator.dart`'s `_date()`), so a formula-only cutoff referencing just the date field would be inaccurately generous for any event with a real start time later in the day; a dedicated kind is also validator-checkable ahead of time rather than failing at runtime on a typo'd function name.
proposedNotImplemented.locationOverlapGuard: NEW 2026-07-26 (CAL.Calendar2.9). Guard kind 9 (guards.md) -- `{ locationField, dateField, timeField?, durationMinutes }`, a HARD guard (blocks the mutation, not a display-only warning) preventing two sibling instances of the same workflow type from sharing a `locationField` value with overlapping `[start, start+durationMinutes)` ranges. Confirmed to need real new engine work, not a cheap formula composition: `source_query.dart`'s `query(...)` grammar supports only one equality condition (no compound filters, no self-exclusion), and the formula language has no generic per-element map/filter to scan a candidate list and compare time ranges from smaller primitives -- this is closer in shape to `effects.md`'s bespoke `recurrence_evaluator.dart` than a one-line addition. Depends on `creationGuardStateKey` above to have anywhere to actually run at creation time.
proposedNotImplemented.actorEqualsFieldGuard: IMPLEMENTED 2026-07-31 (CAL.Notify.1, commit `06f53ed`; validator rules CAL.Notify.2, commit `572b8f6`). Guard kind 10 (guards.md) -- `{ key }`, passing only if `$actor == instanceData[key]` for a scalar (non-list) field. Found while designing a `notification` workflow type's `mark-read` transition: neither `instanceDataEquals` (compares to a fixed literal) nor `actorInList` (list-membership only) can express "the actor must equal this single scalar field's own value." Without it, only-the-recipient-can-dismiss-their-own-notification would be a UI convention, not engine-enforced -- the same category of gap `editGuardEngineEnforcement` above closes for a different call site.
proposedNotImplemented.transitionRelatedOnSuccessEffects: IMPLEMENTED 2026-07-31 (CAL.Notify.1, commit `06f53ed`; validator rules CAL.Notify.2, commit `572b8f6`). Extends `effects.md` op 11 (`transitionRelated`) with an optional `onSuccessEffects: WorkflowEffect[]` field, run only when the resolved target's transition actually succeeds, interpolated against the TARGET instance's own data -- not the instance that declared `transitionRelated`. Found necessary (not a shortcut avoided): an unconditional effect attached directly to the target transition itself (e.g. `respond-going`'s own effects) cannot distinguish "promoted via transitionRelated" from "member manually tapped Going" -- both call the identical transition, so an unconditional notification effect there would wrongly fire on every ordinary self-initiated RSVP too, not just genuine promotions. This is real new engine work, not zero-cost composition, correcting an earlier (wrong) assumption in this session that waitlist-promotion notifications would need no new engine primitives at all.
proposedNotImplemented.notificationWorkflowType: FIXTURE-LOCKED 2026-07-31 (CAL.Notify.3, commit `5c88c7c`) -- App-Shell rendering NOT implemented, deliberately deferred to a new Notifications Experience phase (see the tracker). A new, generic `notification` workflow type -- `unread` (initial) -> `read` (terminal) states, one `mark-read` transition gated by `actorEqualsFieldGuard` above, schema `{ recipientPersonaId, title, body, createdAt }`. Live in the frozen fixture: `respond-maybe`/`respond-declined`'s existing `transitionRelated` effects (waitlist promotion) gained `onSuccessEffects` creating a real notification targeting the promoted row's own `personaId`. Both real validators re-run clean (0/0) against the updated fixture. **Rendering plan superseded 2026-07-31 (CAL.Notify.4, attempted and reverted)**: the original plan (a `renderBindings[].tabId: "calendar"` entry + `rolesForInstance` lambda) was actually wired up and immediately crashed Calendar the moment a real notification instance existed via the genuine waitlist-promotion path -- root cause: Calendar's date-grid projection (`_CalendarEntry`, `part28_engine_native_calendar_surface.dart`) requires every rendered instance to carry a valid `eventDate`, unconditionally, regardless of `cardSurfaceFamily`. Confirmed this is not a Calendar-tab-compatible rendering shape at all. Per the user: notification rendering becomes its own dedicated phase (bell icon / dedicated tab / fixed top-of-tab card surface / FAB are the real candidate patterns, to be researched and decided during that phase's own design pass), which will also own Calendar's eventual integration with it (e.g. event-creator-scheduled reminders), not a bolt-on to the existing date grid.
proposedNotImplemented.transitionInputDialogFields: IMPLEMENTED 2026-07-26 (CAL.Calendar2.1, round 1) but never entered here until now -- a documentation gap, not an implementation gap. `transitions[].inputs[].{visibleWhen,options,modeGroup,modeValue}` (workflow-grammar.md's new `transitions[].inputs` section): a generic, schema-driven dialog (`GenericTransitionInputDialog`) auto-renders a form from any transition's declared `inputs`, replacing the one-off bespoke `_RecurrenceRulePickerDialog` `make-recurring` used to have (now deleted -- one input-collection code path, not two). `visibleWhen` is a live formula evaluated against persisted instance data merged with this dialog's in-progress values; `options` renders chips (single-select for `type: "text"`, multi-select for `type: "list"`); `modeGroup`/`modeValue` groups mutually-exclusive inputs behind one radio choice.
proposedNotImplemented.transitionInputWritesToAndMaxSelections: IMPLEMENTED 2026-07-26 (CAL.Calendar2.1 fix1, commit `58cba6f`). Closes the cardinality gap the implementation agent correctly declined to guess around: `byDayOfWeek` must be multi-select for weekly recurrence but exactly-one-select when paired with the monthly `lastOrNthWeekday` mode (`recurrence_evaluator.dart` enforces `bySetPos` requires `byDayOfWeek.length == 1`), and a single input spec has no way to express mode-conditional cardinality. Adds two fields to `transitions[].inputs[]`: `maxSelections: int?` caps a `type: "list"` + `options` (multi-select chip) input, evicting the oldest pick past the cap -- a UI-side single-select-via-chips convenience, most commonly `1`; `writesTo: string?` overrides the instance-data/`{input.x}` key an entry's value is collected under (default: its own map key), letting two mode-scoped inputs with different shapes share one logical output field since only one is ever visible/relevant at a time. The fixture's `make-recurring` transition now declares `byDayOfWeekWeekly` (unbounded, `visibleWhen: "freq == 'weekly'"`) and `byDayOfWeekMonthly` (`maxSelections: 1`, `modeGroup`/`modeValue` matching the existing `lastOrNthWeekday` radio), both `writesTo: "byDayOfWeek"`.

proposedNotImplemented.notificationDeliveryService: NEW 2026-07-31 (Notifications Experience phase, CAL.Notify2.8). A local-only native OS notification layer, added because this engine has no backend server/push infrastructure anywhere (confirmed: fully local-first, zero network calls in the whole codebase) -- real remote push (FCM/APNs) was explicitly ruled out as requiring a genuinely new backend service. `NotificationDeliveryService` (abstract, one `deliver(notification)` method) + `LocalNotificationDeliveryService` (the only implementation, using the `flutter_local_notifications` plugin) is wired to the single choke point every notification-creating code path already funnels through, so a future real backend can swap the implementation behind the same interface without touching any call site.
